name: Spain — Spanish parties
intro: compare it with Spanish political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Spain: those represented in the Congress of Deputies and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the Congress of Deputies after the July 2023 general election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 350 members. Podemos left the Sumar group in December 2023. Regional parties (ERC, Junts, EH Bildu, PNV, BNG, CC, UPN) are shown as Other.

Podemos.name: Podemos
Podemos.priorities: Affordable housing, Public services, Taxing wealth, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries, Gender equality and feminism
Podemos.description: Left-wing populist party born from the 2011 15-M protests. It was in government with the PSOE from 2020 to 2023, then left the Sumar alliance. It calls for rent controls, public housing and higher taxes on the wealthy, and opposes sending arms to Ukraine.

Sumar.name: Sumar
Sumar.ideologies: Democratic socialism, Green politics, Feminism, Pro-Europeanism
Sumar.priorities: Workers' rights and wages, Affordable housing, Climate action, Public services, Gender equality and feminism
Sumar.description: Left-wing platform led by labour minister Yolanda Díaz, the junior partner in Pedro Sánchez's coalition government. It has raised the minimum wage, pushes for a shorter working week and combines left-wing economics with green and pro-European positions.

PSOE.name: Partido Socialista Obrero Español
PSOE.priorities: Workers' rights and wages, Affordable housing, Gender equality and feminism, Deeper European integration, Climate action
PSOE.description: Spain's oldest party, leading the government under Pedro Sánchez since 2018 with support from regional parties. Socially progressive (it legalised euthanasia and favours abolishing prostitution), strongly pro-European and committed to renewables and phasing out nuclear power.

Volt.name: Volt España
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

PP.name: Partido Popular
PP.priorities: Lower taxes, Unity of Spain, Fighting corruption, Reducing immigration, Fiscal discipline
PP.description: The main party of the Spanish centre-right and the largest in Congress since 2023, though short of a majority. It favours tax cuts, a firm line on Catalan and Basque nationalism and tighter migration control, and wants to keep nuclear plants open.

Vox.name: Vox
Vox.ideologies: National conservatism, Nationalism, Anti-immigration, Soft Euroscepticism
Vox.priorities: Reducing immigration, Unity of Spain, Traditional family values, Security and law and order, Farmers and rural areas
Vox.description: Radical-right party founded by former PP members, now the third force in Congress. It opposes regional autonomy, abortion and euthanasia, defends bullfighting and traditional values, and wants deportations and much less immigration.

SALF.name: Se Acabó La Fiesta
SALF.priorities: Fighting corruption, Security and law and order, Lower taxes, Reducing immigration
SALF.description: Anti-establishment movement founded by the social-media agitator Alvise Pérez, which won three seats in the 2024 European election. It calls for mega-prisons on the Salvadoran model, harsh penalties for corruption and much lower taxes.
